terms.meaning: the web address a page lives at, such as /reminders

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for quick action buttons
sections.what: Brings in the icons, the button component and the page router used by the quick action buttons.
sections.why: The buttons need icons for display and the router to move the user to other pages.

sections.name: actions
sections.title: Definition of the four action buttons
sections.what: Lists the four shortcut buttons shown on the dashboard: Upload Report, Chat with AI, Schedule and Emergency. Each has a label, an icon and a color.
sections.why: Keeps the button list in one place, so the layout below can draw them all with the same code.
sections.watch_out: The id values are used to decide what each click does, so renaming an id here breaks the matching click handler.

sections.name: QuickActions
sections.title: Quick action grid and click handling
sections.what: Draws the four buttons in a grid, two across on phones and four across on larger screens. Clicking Upload Report opens the report upload page, and clicking Schedule opens the reminders page. Chat with AI and Emergency have no click action, so they do nothing when pressed.
sections.why: Gives fast access to the most common tasks from the dashboard home.
sections.watch_out: The Chat with AI and Emergency buttons look active but do nothing. Emergency is a safety feature, so a user expecting a call or alert may get no response.

summary: Four large shortcut buttons for upload, chat, schedule and emergency, shown on the dashboard.
purpose: Gives the patient one-tap access to common tasks.
why: Likely reason: puts the most common tasks at the top of the dashboard. Not fully stated in the code.
how: Holds a fixed list of four actions, each with a label, icon and color. Clicking Upload opens the report upload page. Clicking Schedule opens the reminders page. The Chat with AI and Emergency buttons have no action in this file.
inputs: The fixed action list in the file, and user clicks.
risks: Two buttons do nothing when clicked. A patient who expects the Emergency button to work could be let down. Page paths are typed by hand, so a renamed page breaks navigation without any warning.
debug: If a button does nothing, check the handleAction function for its id. If navigation fails, confirm the target route exists.
